checks.claim: Setup: restricted time (0,1), real completions H_t, H_sp, H, and the tensor identification H=H_t tensor H_sp as a new obligation with non-density covariances.
checks.reason: The hypotheses match the accepted class: d=1,2,3, 0<a<1, alpha+a<2, alpha<d or alpha=d=1. On algebraic tensors the covariance factorizes. Tensors of tests are dense in fixed-support tests by the partition argument in source-operator-convergence Section 4 together with driver bound (5). The map from H_t tensor H_sp onto H is therefore a well-defined unitary, and no density representation of Gamma is needed. H is a closed subspace of H_W because the inclusion of tests is isometric.

checks.claim: C1: the H1 bound ||fg||_Hsp<=sqrt(R_sp)N(f)N(g) follows from bridge (15), and the dyadic sum gives a continuous bilinear H^s x H^s->H_sp for alpha/4<s<1/2.
checks.reason: Taking (f1,f2,f3,f4)=(f,g,f,g) in (15) gives B(fg,fg)<=R0 N(f)^2 N(g)^2, and the bridge proves R_sp=R0. Bernstein gives N(Delta_j f)<=C 2^(alpha j/4)||Delta_j f||_2, with the low block bounded by its L2 norm. Cauchy-Schwarz in j gives sum<=(sum 2^(2j(alpha/4-s)))^(1/2)||f||_H^s, which is finite exactly when s>alpha/4. The range is nonempty because alpha<2-a<2. The sqrt(R_sp) amplitude scales correctly with Gamma. The threshold agrees with the exact scaling L^(alpha/2-2s). Real radial Littlewood-Paley symbols keep inputs inside the accepted real class. Products of H1 functions lie in the completion by polarization and the accepted PSD passage (16).

checks.claim: C1: the signed physical four-linear form on H^s is absolutely convergent, continuous and agrees with the completion on products.
checks.reason: Since sum_j||Delta_j f||_2<infinity, the series converges absolutely a.e. with an L2 majorant. The null-set observation after bridge (1) passes this to both two-point positions nu-a.e. Tonelli and (15) then give int|f1 f2 f3 f4|dnu<=R0 product_i sum_j N(Delta_j f_i)<=C product_i||f_i||_H^s. Multilinearity gives joint continuity. Agreement with the completion follows from the double series and smooth-test pairing, writing a smooth q as q*chi with chi=1 on supp q. The target correctly lists series, representative and null obligations as unproved.

checks.claim: C1: T_sp q=iB(m_R(Gamma*q)) extends to a bounded compact operator-norm map H_sp->K(F), not merely one with compact values, with mask after covariance and constant columns retained.
checks.reason: For state (z,c1,c2) and E-dual w, the second E entry pairs through phi=Lambda^-1 w2, with ||phi||_H1/2=||w2||_H-1/2. The matrix entry is <q,(zeta_R(z1+c1))(zeta_R phi)>_Hsp. Compact-sobolev Proposition 1 with sigma=s, gamma=1/2-s makes H1/2->H^s cutoff multiplication compact. The constant column zeta_R c1 adds a finite-rank part. The bilinear image L of the two unit balls is therefore relatively compact in H_sp, and ||T_sp q||=sup_(k in L)|<q,k>|. For finite orthogonal P_n strongly tending to I, ||T_sp(I-P_n)||<=sup_(k in L)||(I-P_n)k||->0 uniformly on the compact set. So T_sp is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank maps into K(F). This is exactly the required Cameron-map compactness and uses no multiplier on the noise quotient.

checks.reason: Target lines 42-45 and 65 and the crosswalk exclude these explicitly. The compactness argument above uses only the deterministic Cameron map and physical multiplication of state functions, never of raw noise labels.

checks.claim: C2 scalar: K is positive compact on L2 without trace class, H_t->range K^(1/2) is an isometry with mean identification, H_t->L^r is bounded by dual Cauchy-Schwarz and Young, and it is compact by L2 and L^r2 interpolation for all 2<r<2/a.
checks.reason: For a test g, ||g||_Ht^2<=||K||_L^(r/2)(-1,1)||g||_r'^2 by Young, since 1+1/r=2/r+1/r'. Hence ||K*f||_r<=||K||_(r/2)^(1/2)||f||_Ht, with ||K||_(r/2)=(2/(1-ar/2))^(2/r), which is finite iff r<2/a. Truncated kernels are bounded and hence HS, and the near-diagonal error tends to 0 by Schur. No PSD property of truncations is used, and K itself is positive by the accepted Laplace identity. With iota f=K^(1/2)f isometric on H_t, the mean map equals K^(1/2) iota, which is compact into L2. Holder interpolation against bounded L^r2 gives compactness into L^r. The spike scaling confirms failure at r>=2/a. K has infinite trace but stays compact.

checks.claim: C2 vector-valued: dimension-free Hilbert bound, strong measurability, and raw H_sp labels passing through spatial covariance exactly once.
checks.reason: For G in L^r'(H_sp), ||G||_H^2<=int int|t-u|^-a||G(t)||||G(u)||<=||K||_(r/2)||G||_L^r'(Hsp)^2 with no dependence on dimension. Therefore J:H->L^r((0,1);H_sp), the raw time convolution, is bounded with norm at most ||K||_(r/2)^(1/2). Separability and reflexivity of the Hilbert fiber give duality and Pettis measurability. Then T=T_sp J applies Gamma once, consistent with the accepted h_s definition. The non-vector guard correctly shows J alone is noncompact when H_sp is infinite-dimensional.

checks.claim: C2: T:H->L^r((0,1);K(F)) is compact through spatial finite-rank approximation, with no scalar compact tensor infinite identity error.
checks.reason: ||T-T_sp P_n J||<=||T_sp(I-P_n)||||J||->0. Also T_sp P_n J Psi=sum_(i<=n)(K*tau_i)T_sp q_i, where tau_i=(id tensor <.,q_i>)Psi is bounded H->H_t and K*:H_t->L^r is compact. Each approximant is a finite sum of compact maps, so the limit T is compact. C1's norm approximation is genuinely necessary, as the statement says.

checks.claim: C3: exact block Cameron shift on actual given-W fast pullbacks with sqrt(delta) covariance factor, and projection in slow raw H before pullback.
checks.reason: Raw-block (2),(5),(6) give E[W_(delta,m)(f)W(Phi)]=delta^(a/2)int f(u,x)h(s_m+delta u,x)du dx, and g_delta delta^(a/2)=sqrt(delta). For Y_J=W(I-P_J), <T_(delta,m)f,(I-P_J)Psi> gives the display with (I-P_J)Psi. Conjugation S_F(-v)T(...)S_F(v) matches H_m in (3). The accepted statement is for positive smooth tests; signed and complete directions follow by linearity and continuity, since both sides are bounded in Psi. The target marks this as an obligation. checks.claim: C3 exponents: 1/2<theta<1-a/2 within the driver range, 1/(1-theta)<r<2/a, 1/theta<=p<2 imply p<r and consistency with C2.
checks.reason: theta<1-a/2 is equivalent to 1/(1-theta)<2/a, so r exists. theta>1/2 gives 1/(1-theta)>2, hence r>2 lies in C2's range and p<2<r. 1/theta<2 makes the p range nonempty. checks.claim: C3: local L^r primitive estimate, weighted finite Holder and cardinality give delta cancellation and the uniform bound C_(R,B)sqrt(delta)epsilon_J.
checks.reason: With t_m=||T Phi||_L^r(I_m;K(F)) and I_m the true interval, Holder gives ||A_m(u)-A_m(u')||<=C_B^2 sqrt(delta)|u-u'|^(1-1/r)delta^(-1/r)t_m, and 1-1/r>theta. Zero start and fixed B give the Ctheta norm with the same factors. Sum_m t_m^p<=(N+1)^(1-p/r)(sum t_m^r)^(p/r), and N+1<=2/(delta B). Therefore (delta sum||A_m||^p)^(1/p)<=C sqrt(delta)delta^(-1/r)delta^(1/p)(2/(delta B))^(1/p-1/r)||T Phi||_L^r, whose net delta power is exactly sqrt(delta). Stress tests agree: the coherent equilibrium direction is sharp at sqrt(delta), and a single-block spike gives delta^(1/p+(1-a)/2)<=sqrt(delta) for p<=2/a. T and P_J live in slow variables and do not depend on delta, so uniformity is genuine. No fixed-delta transfer is imported.

checks.reason: T compact from Hilbert H to Banach L^r(K(F)) makes the adjoint compact by Schauder, and ||T(I-P_J)||=||(I-P_J)T*||->0 because I-P_J tends strongly to 0 uniformly on compact sets. Finite-rank approximation gives the same result. P_J need not be tensor-adapted.

checks.claim: C3: Bochner conjugation with strong free group and adjoint and compact integrands, with no operator-norm time continuity assumed.
checks.reason: For compact K, v->S_F(-v)K S_F(v) is norm continuous, by strong continuity of S_F and of its Hilbert adjoint uniformly on compact sets. Simple-function approximation in the separable K(F) (raw-block Section 3) makes the conjugated L^r integrand strongly measurable into K(F). The operator integral is therefore a true Bochner integral. The target records this as an obligation and does not assume norm continuity of S_F.
